A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Code Execution as Grounded Supervision for LLM Reasoning. All 12 pages, including Appendices A–D, Figure 1, and Tables 1–10, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen3 fine-tuning evaluations, benchmark accuracies, reasoning-correctness assessments, and token-length analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and their outcomes, including Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B benchmark results in Tables 1 and 6.

M1.justification: Both versions use Snoop execution traces, LLM translation into natural-language reasoning, and supervised fine-tuning. Section 2 and the method's prompt templates in Table 8 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use PyEdu-R for supervision and evaluate LiveBench coding, math, and reasoning, plus MATH500, BBH, AGIEval, and GPQA. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 6 retain No Training, Code Generation (Code), Raw Execution Trace (Raw Trace), and CodeI/O. Comparator membership in the correctness, token-length, and case-study comparisons also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 3.1 and 3.3 and Appendix A retain identical model configurations, LiveBench release, training and decoding settings, filtering procedures, and the 200-sample intermediate-reasoning assessment.

E4.justification: Both retain the correctness and token-length analyses in Section 3.3 and Tables 2, 3, and 5, plus the permutation and Josephus case studies in Tables 9 and 10. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both use the same reporting of point accuracies and token statistics. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative cases are unchanged. For example, the proposed method retains average accuracies of 58.5 for Qwen3-4B (Table 1) and 61.5 for Qwen3-8B (Table 6), with identical correctness and token-length results.

T1.justification: Section 2 retains the same generation factorization and mathematical definitions of execution traces and translated-trace datasets. No assumptions, derivations, theoretical results, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion preserve the same claims about scalable execution-grounded supervision, transferable reasoning, accurate reasoning traces, and reduced inference token use.

C2.justification: Interpretations of baseline performance, grounding, and reduced repetition are unchanged. Both limitations sections retain the restriction to tasks expressible through executable code and the possibility of imperfect LLM translation.

D1.justification: Appendix A, Tables 4 and 8, and Appendix D retain identical hardware, hyperparameters, filtering instructions, generation/evaluation configurations, prompts, and licenses. The code and data repository disclosure is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and reference entries are unchanged. Section 4 preserves the same positioning relative to reasoning distillation and execution-based approaches, including its distinction from CodeI/O.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgment section thanking reviewers and identifying funding sources. Footnotes replace 'Appendix' with 'Section' when referring to B, A.2, and A.3; the scientific narrative is otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment causes text and table reflow on pages 5–8, including changed placement of Tables 4 and 5. Appendix code and case-study tables have small spacing changes; Figure 1 and all table contents and captions are retained.

improvement.justification: The methods, empirical evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations remain unchanged, including the appendices. The added acknowledgment and funding disclosure provide attribution, while the other edits concern cross-reference wording and layout; these do not materially change the paper's overall quality.
